title: Onramp Spark Sessions and Labs — Outline (Draft)
summary: Working draft: lightweight, instructor-friendly lab catalogue and schedule for 45–90 minute interactive "spark sessions" that get new SDK users from zero to a deployable prototype. Focus on minimal friction, deterministic outcomes, and observable metrics for early telemetry collection.
audience: software engineers and ML engineers trying Redwood API/SDK for the first time; internal solutions engineers running onboarding sessions with customers; developer advocates running workshops.
goals:
- get a developer to a reproducible hello-world LLM flow in <= 45 mins
- collect consistent telemetry (latency, token counts, cost estimates) from participants
- create lab artifacts that are runnable locally and in a sandboxed hosted account
- make the path easily runnable during sales-assisted POCs and self-serve onboarding
workshop-format-options: - Spark (45m): 10m intro + 25m guided lab + 10m QA\n- Deep Lab (90m): 20m intro + 60m guided lab + 10m wrap\n- Async kit: self-study repo + one recorded guided walkthrough (~20m)
session-principles:
- deterministic outcomes: single, small repo with pinned deps and a test fixture
- low setup cost: CLI script to provision sandbox API key or use temp tokens
- observability from day one: built-in sample telemetry hooks that post results to a shared dashboard
- hardware-aware examples: include one snippet showing cost/latency tradeoffs (e.g., batch=1 vs batch=8)
- failure-mode exercises: intentionally trigger a quota/latency fallback to demonstrate graceful degradation
lab-catalogue:
1) Hello-Gen: minimal text generation
   - objective: call Redwood text-generation, stream tokens, print latency & token counts
   - deliverable: run script greet.py and see streaming output; evaluate 2 prompt variations
   - learning: streaming API, token accounting, basic retry policy

2) ChatFlow: chat state + function-calling stub
   - objective: local chat loop that calls a toy function (math or db lookup) via tool-calling schema
   - deliverable: chat-demo.py with a simulated function; show structured JSON outputs and function results
   - learning: function-calling pattern, structured output enforcement, response validation

3) Embeddings-Retrieve: embeddings + vector retrieve (local index)
   - objective: index 20 docs, run semantic search, compare embedding models and distance metrics
   - deliverable: small notebook that computes recall/precision on a tiny QA set and reports latency
   - learning: embedding costs, dimensionality impact, local FAISS vs hosted vector db notes

4) Quantize-and-Profile (advanced lab)
   - objective: run a supported model variant with/without quantization flags to show CPU/GPU tradeoffs
   - deliverable: profile script that outputs per-token CPU/GPU time and memory footprint
   - learning: quantization effect on throughput & quality, how Redwood recommends profiles
prework-checklist:
- confirm SDK installed (pip/npms)
- have API key or sandbox token script ready (provision.sh)
- git clone starter repo and run ./setup-local.sh
- optional: Docker installed if running containerized lab
automation-and-scripts: - provision.sh: creates sandbox API key, config file, test dataset\n- run-lab.sh: one-command entry that runs the selected lab and captures telemetry to ./results.json\n- collect-telemetry.py: posts metrics to internal dashboard or Slack channel for trainer visibility
telemetry-contracts: - required: total API calls, token in/out, per-call latency (p50/p95), model name, quantization flag\n- recommended: CPU/GPU time, peak memory, batch size, prompt length distribution\n- format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with standard keys to simplify ingestion
sample-quickstart-sketch:
1) Intro slide (5m): why SDK? demo of streaming + function call
2) Run Hello-Gen (15m): participants run the script, tweak prompt, observe streaming tokens and token counts
3) Telemetry check (5m): trainer shows aggregated dashboard with sample data from earlier runs
4) ChatFlow (20m): guided extension, explain function-calling and validation
5) Wrap + next steps (5m): point to deeper labs and repo
sprint-tasks: Create starter repo with 4 labs and pin deps
Write provision.sh and run-lab.sh with idempotent behavior
Add telemetry hooks and a simple ingestion endpoint (internal-only)
Write instructor notes with expected time per section and troubleshooting tips
Draft one-page cheat-sheet for engineers (commands, common errors, telemetry keys)
risks-and-mitigations: - risk: high friction during environment setup -> mitigation: containerized runner and one-click sandbox token\n- risk: noisy telemetry from environment variability -> mitigation: include a small synthetic benchmark fixture inside each lab\n- risk: customers copy demo prompts verbatim into production -> mitigation: clear callouts and best-practice guardrails in lab notes
open-questions: Should sandbox tokens be single-use or time-limited? (security tradeoffs)
Do we require participants to use Docker, or provide a host-run option for non-dev attendees?
What is minimal set of telemetry we can collect without PII concerns?
next-steps:

- implement repo skeleton and provision scripts (owner: Marco)
- create a short trainer slide deck (owner: Priya)

body:
Notes / rough script (freeform)

Opening (1–2 mins): quick purpose statement: "get you comfortable enough with Redwood SDK that you can ship a prototype in a day". Stress the path: streaming -> chat -> embeddings -> profiling. Keep energy high, demo first to show instant feedback.

Trainer tips:
- Run through the whole lab once locally before a session; note any flaky steps.
- Have a backup recording of the whole run in case of live infra issues.
- Encourage participants to copy-paste commands rather than typing; saves time.

Failure-mode script (very short): intentionally set an extremely short token limit or bad model name to trigger error handling; show how SDK surfaces the error and how the rectangle (fallback policy) re-routes to a smaller model. Good teaching moment about graceful degradation.

Prompt engineering microtask: give two prompt primes and ask participants to pick one and refine in 5m to improve relevance. Have a tiny rubric: 1) clarity 2) context length 3) expected format.

Github repo layout idea:
- /labs/hello_gen/greet.py
- /labs/chatflow/chat-demo.py
- /labs/embeddings/notebook.ipynb
- /labs/profile/profile.py
- /scripts/provision.sh
- /scripts/run-lab.sh
- /trainer/instructor-notes.md

Sample commands (to be copyable):
- ./scripts/provision.sh --env=sandbox
- ./scripts/run-lab.sh hello_gen --output=results/hello_gen.ndjson
- python3 tools/collect-telemetry.py --file=results/hello_gen.ndjson --post-to=ingest.test.internal

End notes: Keep labs tiny and ritualized. The measurable success criteria for the program: percentage of participants who ship a prototype to staging within 48 hours and shares telemetry. Track that across pilots.

Links / references: include confluence page (DX-ONRAMP-boarding), Jira ticket DX-412, and the pending GH PR for the starter repo.
